newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Sweden cannot impose TV ad ban on other states.
newsitem.headline: Court says Sweden cannot impose TV ad ban on other states.

text.p: The European Court of Justice told Sweden on Wednesday it could not apply its national ban on advertising aimed at children to broadcasters based in Britain.

The Televison Without Frontiers directive places responsibility for TV content on the member state from which programmes and advertisements are broadcast, and prevents the receiving member states from imposing additional restrictions.

"A receiving state may not stop retransmission of a broadcast coming from another member state or apply provisions having the specific purpose of controlling the content of televison advertising directed at minors," the court said.

The aim of the directive is to open up broadcasting between member states, the court said, and therefore states cannot introduce increased restrictions on transmissions in an area which the directive has addressed, such as advertising aimed at children.
However, the court said member states may penalize advertisers for broadcasting misleading information, no matter where the transmission originates.

The court noted that EU law does exist which permits member states to take measures against misleading advertising, as long as those measures do not prevent the retransmission of broadcasts originating in another state.
The court's decision recognizes a member state's right to protect consumers, even if doing so creates a restriction to free trade in the Community.
The Swedish Marketing Practices Law also prohibits TV advertising "contrary to good commercial practice or otherwise unfair towards consumers or other traders," according to the court.

The court said Sweden could legislate against false advertising originating in another member state because advertising time purchased between member states constitutes a provision of a service, and because fair trading and consumer protection are overriding interests to free trade.
Joined cases C-34/95, C-35/95, C-36/95

application for an interpretation of the TV without Frontiers directive 89/552/EEC and article 30 or article 59 on the restriction of advertising broadcast from another member state
THE COURT hereby rules

1. Council directive 89/552/EEC on the coordination of certain provisions laid down by law, regulation or administrative action in member states concerning the pursuit of television broadcasting activities does not preclude a member state from taking, pursuant to general legislation on protection of consumers against misleading advertising, measures against an advertiser in relation to television advertising broadcast from another member state, provided that those measures do not prevent the retransmission, as such, in its territory of television broadcasts coming from that other member state.

2. On a proper construction of article 30 of the EC teaty, a member state is not precluded from taking, on the basis of provisions of its domestic legislation, measures against an advertiser in relation to television advertising, provided that those provisions affect in the same way, in law and in fact, the marketing of domestic products and of those from other member states, are necessary for meeting overriding requirements of general public importance of one of the aims laid down in article 36 of the EC treaty, are proportionate for that purpose, and those aims or overriding requirements could not be met by measures less restrictive of intra-Community trade.

3. On a proper construction of article 59 of the EC treaty, a member state is not precluded from taking, on the basis of provisions of its domestic legislation, measures against an advertiser in relation to television advertising. However, it is for the national court to determine whether these provisions are necessary for meeting overriding requirements of general public importance or one of the aims stated in article 56 of the EC treaty, whether they are proportionate for that purpose and whether those aims or overriding requirements could be met by measures less restrictive of intra-Community trade.

4. Directive 89/552/EEC is to be interpreted as precluding the application to television broadcasts from other member states of a provision of a domestic broadcasting law which provides that advertisements broadcast in commercial breaks on television must not be designed to attract the attention of children under 12 years of age.
